1.w: Do not boast about tomorrow for, you do not know what a day will bring forth.

2.w: Let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth—a foreigner, and not your own lips.

3.w: The heaviness of a stone and the weight of the sand—and the anger of a fool [is] heavier than both of them.

4.w: The cruelty of rage and the flood of a nostril—and who can stand before the face of jealousy?

5.w: Better [is] an uncovered rebuke than love hidden.

6.w: Faithful [are] the wounds of one who loves, and abundant are the kisses of one hating.

7.w: A soul satiated would trample a honeycomb, and [to] a hungry soul, everything bitter [is] sweet.

8.w: Like a bird wandering from her nest, so [is] a man wandering from his place.

9.w: Oil and incense gladden the heart, and the sweetness of one’s friend is from the counsel of the soul.

10.w: Do not forsake your friend, and the friend of your father, and do not enter the house of your brother in the day of your calamity; better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.

11.w: Be wise, my son, and gladden my heart, that I may return a word to the one reproaching me.

12.w: A prudent one sees evil [coming]; he hides himself; simple ones pass along, [and] they are punished.

13.w: Take his garment when a stranger posts security, and hold it in pledge for a foreign woman.

14.w: The one blessing his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it will be counted [as] a curse for him.

15.w: A continual dripping in a day of rain, and a woman of quarrels are alike—

16.w: hiding her is hiding the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand.

17.w: Iron is sharpened by iron, and a man sharpens the face of his friend.

18.w: One keeping watch over a fig tree will eat its fruit, and the one guarding his master will be honored.

19.w: As [in] the water the face [is] to the face, so the heart of the man [is] to the man.

20.w: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and the eyes of the man are never satisfied.

21.w: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, so is a man by the mouth of one who praises him.

22.w: Though you may pound a fool in the mortar, in the midst of the grain with the pestle, his folly will not turn away from him.

23.w: Be sure to know the faces of your flock, [and] set your heart to your herds,

24.w: for riches [are] not forever, nor [is] a diadem for all generations.

25.w: The hay is uncovered, and the tender grass is visible, and the herbs of the mountains are gathered.

26.w: The lambs [are] for your clothing, and the goats the price of field,

27.w: and enough milk of goats [is] for your foor, for the food of your house and the life of your maidservants.
